inline_comments.comment: The three new values are inserted in the wrong order for the stated design intent. `getMostCriticalStatusValue` iterates `statusPriority` from start to finish and returns the last match (highest index), so the highest-indexed value wins. With `['affected'(3), 'modified'(4), 'new'(5)]` the effective priority is `new > modified > affected`. But the PR description and the inline story comment both document `affected > modified > new` (affected should be most critical). The correct insertion order should be the inverse — `'status-value:new'`, then `'status-value:modified'`, then `'status-value:affected'` — so that `affected` sits closest to `warning` and therefore wins in a comparison.

The test description says 'should rank affected above modified' and the assertion is `.toBe('status-value:affected')`, but this contradicts the `statusPriority` array as written in this PR. With `affected` at index 3 and `modified` at index 4, `getMostCriticalStatusValue(['affected', 'modified', 'success'])` returns `'status-value:modified'` (the later/higher-indexed element wins via the reduce). The assertion will fail at runtime. This inconsistency is a direct symptom of the ordering bug in `statusPriority` — fix the array order (see comment on `status.tsx`) and then update the test name to accurately describe the intended behaviour.

`StatusIconMap` maps `'status-value:new'`, `'status-value:modified'`, and `'status-value:affected'` to `null`, so the `if (icon)` guard downstream will suppress the status button on individual story leaf nodes entirely. Only group/component nodes will surface change-detection status (via the `showBranchStatus` path). This is an asymmetry: a group shows "modified" but the specific story within it has no visible indicator. If this is intentional (e.g., change-detection is only meaningful at the aggregate level), add a brief comment explaining the design decision so future contributors don't wonder why these statuses have icons in `getStatus` but are silenced here.

The inline comment states `// priority ordering (most critical wins): error > warning > affected > modified > new`, but the actual `statusPriority` array (as written in this PR) makes `new` the most critical of the three, not `affected`. This comment will mislead contributors verifying the story's behaviour. Fix either the array order (so `affected` wins as documented) or the comment (to reflect `new > modified > affected`).

`changeDetection?: boolean` is declared with `@default true` but is never read or enforced anywhere in this PR. Per project conventions, an opt-out flag (`@default true`) must also have its default set explicitly in the common preset (`code/core/src/core-server/presets/common-preset.ts`) so that standard truthy guards work correctly without scattering `!== false` checks at call sites. As written, this field is dead code. If the implementation is deferred to a follow-up PR, add a comment noting that — otherwise remove the field until the consuming code is in place.

The diff adds group-aggregation propagation tests for `'status-value:new'` and `'status-value:affected'` but not for `'status-value:modified'`. Since all three are introduced together and the other two have symmetric coverage, add an analogous `it('should propagate status-value:modified through group aggregation', ...)` case to ensure `modified` bubbles up through the component/group hierarchy correctly.

general_comments.comment: There is a three-way contradiction between the PR description, the story comment, and the implementation for priority ordering. The PR description says `error > warning > affected > modified > new` (affected most critical of the new three). The `StatusesChangeDetectionPriority` story comment repeats the same ordering. But the `statusPriority` array inserts them as `[..., 'affected', 'modified', 'new', ...]`, which — because `getMostCriticalStatusValue` returns the last/highest-indexed match — produces `new > modified > affected`. Before merging, align all three sources: either reverse the array insertion order to match the stated `affected > modified > new` semantic, or explicitly decide that `new > modified > affected` is correct and update every comment and test description to match.

The `StatusesNew`, `StatusesModified`, `StatusesAffected`, `StatusesMixed`, and `StatusesChangeDetectionPriority` stories all delegate their `play` function to the generic `waitForChecklistWidget`. None of them assert that the new status icons actually appear in the sidebar tree, that the expected colour/icon is rendered, or that group nodes aggregate the status correctly. Adding targeted DOM assertions (e.g. `canvas.getAllByTestId('tree-status-button')` combined with `.not.toHaveTextContent(...)`) would prevent regressions in the new icon/colour rendering paths and satisfy the project guideline that story `play` functions assert both what should be present and what should be absent.
